clue.text: Free translation of Braille

indicators.note: a translation renders the word in another form, so the letters of the name Braille are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loose rendering of a text written in Braille.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean unrestricted or generous, as in a free interpretation.

clue.text: Duties could cause seaman to scowl outwardly

indicators.note: the scowl word sits on the outside, wrapped around the seaman

parts.note: to lour is to frown or scowl
AB, able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Tasks that might make a sailor frown.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is work, the tasks or duties one performs.

clue.text: Thumb through book and files before start of election

parts.note: files are lines or rows, as in rank and file

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word election is used

explanation.surface: Leafing through a book and records ahead of a poll.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse is to look casually through a book, much like thumbing its pages.

clue.text: Single-storey building in Honshu, with acre to be ploughed

indicators.note: ploughing turns the soil over, so the letters of the two words are churned up

explanation.surface: A farm building on a Japanese island set in an acre of land for tilling.
explanation.walkthrough: Honshu is the largest island of Japan; 'with' just joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch house is a long, low one-storey dwelling of the American type.

clue.text: Helplessly drunk, failing to start game

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, so it does not begin

parts.note: blotto is slang for completely drunk

explanation.surface: Someone too inebriated to get a game going.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance, a form of bingo or lottery.

clue.text: Mitchell, say, made stage entrance tackling lead in rep

indicators.note: the stage-entrance phrase takes on, or grips, the other letter in its middle

parts.note: an actor who enters the stage came on

indicators.note: the leading letter of rep

explanation.surface: An actor called Mitchell walks on stage in a repertory play, taking on the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mitchell, say' looks like a surname to be defined, but the answer is a first name, that of the actor Cameron Mitchell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron is a given name, as borne by the American actor Cameron Mitchell.

clue.text: Hebe, perhaps, caught on horseback by messenger

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a jockey who is riding is said to be up
a bearer is one who carries a message

explanation.surface: The goddess Hebe is caught riding behind a courier.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Hebe poured nectar for the gods, serving as their cup-bearer; 'perhaps' marks her as an example.

clue.text: Soldiers round a base

indicators.note: the soldiers stand around the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: men is a common term for soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops gathering around a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Base and mean are both adjectives for something low, ignoble or contemptible.

clue.text: Cut short waiter with dry humour

indicators.note: cutting up the letters breaks them apart and re-forms them
the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before the trim

explanation.surface: Shortchanging a waiter with a dry joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes R from WAITER to give WAITE; with DRY, 'Cut' rearranges WAITEDRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready wit is quick, sharp humour delivered on the spot.

clue.text: Put in order for a number in demand

indicators.note: the article and the number go inside the word for demand

parts.note: to need is to require or demand
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Tidied up because a certain figure was called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatened is a past tense meaning tidied or arranged in order.

clue.text: British have roast

parts.note: to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: The British do like their Sunday roast.
explanation.definitionFit: To brown meat is to cook or roast it until it colours.

clue.text: Finest fruit for leader

parts.note: top means best or finest
a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: Choosing the best fruit for the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is a slang phrase for the boss or most important person.

clue.text: Natural should, once trained

indicators.note: trained means reshaped, as a plant is trained, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A born talent who ought to have had some coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Unschooled means untaught, so natural rather than acquired by learning.

clue.text: For the most part, extremely active publicity

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: hyper means overexcited or extremely active

explanation.surface: Mostly frantic promotional activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is exaggerated promotion or publicity.

clue.text: Bad backache — NY taxi required

indicators.note: bad suggests a corrupted, jumbled version of these letters

explanation.surface: A painful back means you need a New York cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney cab is the formal name for a licensed taxi.

clue.text: Tending to be cautious in blimp?

definitions.meaning: describes someone averse to change and risk
Colonel Blimp, a cartoon figure, embodies a pompous, reactionary outlook, the quality found in such a person

explanation.surface: Is a cautious attitude found in an airship?
explanation.walkthrough: A blimp is an airship, but Colonel Blimp was a cartoon character standing for pompous reactionary views; this political quality is what you find in a blimp.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative means averse to change, cautious, and is the label for a Blimp-like reactionary.

clue.text: Trace a Hitchcock film

definitions.meaning: a slight hint, as in a touch of garlic
the 1941 Alfred Hitchcock thriller starring Cary Grant

explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion can mean a faint trace, and is also the title of a Hitchcock film.

clue.text: Avoids when negotiating black spot

indicators.note: the word for when gets around the other letters, as one negotiates a bend

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
B is an abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a stain is a spot or mark

explanation.surface: Someone steers clear while in talks about a dark blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from something, so abstains means avoids.

clue.text: Party member in protest meeting about one who's been disloyal

parts.note: a demo is a protest demonstration
C is short for circa, about
a rat is a traitor or turncoat

explanation.surface: A party member at a protest rally talks of a defector.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat is a member of the Democratic Party.

clue.text: Discipline in the water — brother given direction by oarsman

parts.note: east is a compass direction
the stroke is the rower who sets the pace in a boat

explanation.surface: A brother taking instructions from a rower on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaststroke is one of the swimming disciplines contested in races.

clue.text: Special gift adult left in shelter

indicators.note: the two letters go inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A special present for a grown-up abandoned in a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural gift or aptitude.

clue.text: Mountain girl in Lancers' home?

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain peak
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl from the hills living in a cavalry quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bengal Lancers were a famous Indian cavalry regiment, so Bengal was their home.

clue.text: Extreme left-winger to run

definitions.meaning: to move at a jogging pace

explanation.definitionFit: A Trot is slang for a Trotskyist, and to trot is to run steadily.

clue.text: Awful mistakes during almost all of major musical

indicators.note: the jumbled letters come within the shortened word
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: major is a musical key, as in C major

indicators.note: awful signals a terrible, jumbled version of the letters

explanation.surface: Dreadful blunders ruin most of a major show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major' stands for a key, as in C major; 'almost all of' drops its last letter, and 'Awful' rearranges the letters of mistakes to go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiss Me, Kate is Cole Porter's musical based on The Taming of the Shrew.

clue.text: Authority to make a statement in case

parts.note: to say is to state something
so can mean provided that, on condition, as in 'so it rains'

explanation.surface: Power to speak out on a legal matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Say-so means the right or authority to decide, as in on my say-so.

clue.text: Whip-round for famous orator

parts.note: a cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A collection taken for a celebrated speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip-round' looks like a collection, but splits into whip and round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder was a Roman statesman celebrated for his oratory.

clue.text: Actually elected one occupying property

parts.note: a winning candidate is in

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the property word

parts.note: realty is real estate, property
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A winning candidate moving into a house.
explanation.definitionFit: In reality means in fact, actually.

clue.text: Long-serving comedy character, 100 on third of August

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
the on side is the leg side in cricket

indicators.note: the third letter of August

explanation.surface: A veteran sitcom figure reaches a century on the third of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Clegg was a character in Last of the Summer Wine, a BBC sitcom that ran for 37 years; in cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Clegg was a mainstay of the very long-running British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine.

clue.text: Group unhappy making record

parts.note: a set is a group
down means low, sad

explanation.surface: A gloomy band producing an album.
explanation.definitionFit: To set down is to record in writing.

clue.text: M25, maybe — what's said about small section?

indicators.note: the spoken word goes around the small piece

parts.note: oral means spoken
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: A question about part of the London motorway network.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway ring round London, known as the London Orbital.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road circles a city; the M25 is an example.
